messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — CI started failing on the attention-kernel branch after we added the new fused-attn kernels. Build artifacts are ~3MB larger on cuda_11.8 LTO builder and the nightlies are timing out on storage.
alex: Ugh. Is that from extra PTX sections or duplicate fatbins for multiple sm targets?
tj: I ran `cuobjdump --list` on the artifact and it shows multiple `fatbin` blocks: sm_70, sm_75, sm_80, and ptx. Looks like we dropped a plain `--fatbin` collapse step.
sam: Can you paste the nvcc invocation? I suspect our CMake `CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` expansion is generating `-gencode` entries we don't actually need.
maria: Here's the command captured in the CI logs:
```
nvcc -O3 -gencode arch=compute_70,code=sm_70 -gencode arch=compute_75,code=sm_75 -gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -Xcompiler -fPIC -Xlinker --gc-sections -Xlinker -O1 -Xlinker -s -c fused_attn.cu
```
maria: We also pass `-rdc=true` for device linking; that might prevent some strip/GC steps.
infra-bot: Build 4827 failed: artifact size 18.9MB (limit 16.0MB) — size-gate triggered :warning:
alex: Two paths: 1) reduce arch list to supported target(s) in CI, 2) split per-sm artifacts, or 3) add a size gate exemption for attention kernels while we land better compiler flags.
tj: Splitting per-sm increases matrix runs and overall CI time. I'd rather prune the arch list to `sm_80,sm_86` for our GPU fleet and keep ptx out unless needed.
jen: Is ptx required? We used to build ptx for forward-compat but it inflates fatbins a lot.
sam: PTX only helps when running on future archs; for Dedicated/Hosted we control hw, so we can be conservative. Proposal: CI builds two variants: `compat` (wide arch list) on nightly, and `fast` (narrow) for PRs.
alex: Agree. For PRs we keep `-gencode=compute_80,code=sm_80` and `-gencode=compute_86,code=sm_86`. Nightly can include ptx+legacy sm_70.
maria: Also noticed `-lineinfo` was accidentally left on in one CMake override — that adds debug symbols. Removing it drops ~400KB per object.
tj: Can we change the toolchain to call `cuobjdump --strip` or run `nvlink` with `--strip-debug`? I want to avoid ad hoc postprocessing.
sam: nvcc flags to try: `-Xlinker --gc-sections -Xfatbin -compress-all` (if supported), and `--relocatable-device-code=false` for builds that don't need rdc.
jen: We should also gate any change that touches `CMakeLists.txt` with a size regression job. Add a CI job that compares new artifact size vs artifact baseline and fails if >10%.
infra-bot: New CI job created: artifact-size-checker (runs on PRs). Threshold env: ARTIFACT_MAX_PCT=110.
alex: For long-term, let's track per-kernel symbol tables. The new fused-attn kernels include duplicated static tables in each CU. We can move shared tables to a single device symbol to dedupe.
maria: Good call — that's a refactor but will solve runtime memory and disk bloat.
tj: Short term action items:
- PR: narrow arch list for PR CI (sam)
- PR: remove accidental `-lineinfo` (maria)
- Task: add artifact-size-checker job (infra)
- RFC: kernel symbol dedupe plan (alex)
sam: I'll open the PR for the CI matrix change today, link to this thread.
maria: Thanks — please tag me on the PR. If CI still fails I'll create a temporary size-exemption for the feature branch but want that to be rare. :face_with_monocle:
alex: One more note — if we disable `rdc`, some kernels that rely on separate CU linking will break. We should run a smoke test (small inference run) as part of the PR if `rdc` is toggled.
infra-bot: Smoke tests queued for PR #1125 — target runners: cuda-11.8-sm80, cuda-12.1-sm86.
jen: Great. Keep CI changes minimal for now and prioritize the symbol dedupe RFC.
maria: Yep. I'll start a short RFC draft for the symbol consolidation, focusing on exposing a shared const buffer in device link stage.
sam: Cool — ping here when RFC is up. :thumbsup:
